The angles of ${0}^{∘},\,{30}^{∘},$ and ${60}^{∘}$ are special, and their trigonometric ratios have the particular values

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡{0}^{∘}=0,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\,\operatorname{tan}⁡{60}^{∘}=\sqrt{3}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡{0}^{∘}+\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}+\operatorname{tan}⁡{60}^{∘} & = \\ 0+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\sqrt{3} & = \\ \frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}. & \end{aligned}
$$
